source_title: Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Based Dexterous Manipulation on Humanoids

ai_summary.one_liner: A four-part recipe combines robot-model autotuning, contact/object rewards, specialist-to-generalist learning, and depth-position perception for real humanoid dexterous manipulation.
ai_summary.problem: High-dimensional contact control is difficult to explore, while robot modeling and visual distribution gaps obstruct transfer to hardware.
ai_summary.solution: Calibrate simulator parameters against joint tracking, initialize with brief human play states, train PPO specialists, and distill successful trajectories into a depth-and-position Diffusion Policy.
ai_summary.key_result: The best task policies achieve 62.3% grasp-and-reach, 80% box lift, and 52.5% bimanual handover across test objects, with ten trials per object. Separate ten-trial modality ablations are not these overall rates.
limitations: Full success demonstrations are avoided, but task-aware initialization still uses under 30 seconds of human play data per task.
Dynamic transfer relies on conventional domain randomization; handover remains weaker.
Hardware reliability and limited active hand degrees of freedom constrain dexterity.
Three task families and best-policy evaluation provide limited evidence for broadly general manipulation.

research_gaps.question: How can dynamic contact behavior transfer more reliably than with conventional domain randomization, especially for bimanual handover?
How can reward construction incorporate stronger human priors while preserving the efficiency of simulation learning?
Can the framework exploit more reliable hands with richer active degrees of freedom?
How stable are the gains across unseen task families, camera placements, and seeds when the total human setup effort is included?

future_directions: Improve contact-dynamics identification and adaptation for faster coordinated handovers.
Study demonstrations or other human priors as structured reward-design inputs.
Evaluate more capable and reliable multi-fingered hands.
Measure seed-averaged transfer and total setup effort across broader tasks and sensing arrangements.

relations.note: Appendix D trains a generalist with Diffusion Policy on success-filtered trajectories generated by the RL specialists.
RialTo is explicitly cited as reference [55] in the supplied v1 paper. Both study manipulation transfer through simulation, using different supervision and scene-modeling strategies.

A retrospective reading connection requested alongside this paper: both address real/sim alignment for manipulation, but this recipe calibrates humanoid hardware and learns skills while SimFoundry automates scene generation and policy evaluation. No citation or direct benchmark claim.
